transitive.label: With or without an object
transitive.technical: The verb has a transitive and an intransitive use. The transitive use takes avere and the intransitive use takes essere.
transitive.explanation: This verb can be used with a direct object or without one. With an object it takes avere. Without one, the thing that changes is the subject, and it takes essere.

weather.label: Weather verb
weather.technical: A verb for weather or the time of day. Both auxiliaries are correct with no change in meaning.
weather.explanation: Verbs about the weather can take either auxiliary, and the meaning is the same. Essere is the more traditional choice.
weather.essere: Correct, same meaning as avere. The more traditional choice.

modal.label: Takes the auxiliary of the next verb
modal.technical: A modal verb takes the auxiliary of the verb it governs.
modal.explanation: This verb takes the same auxiliary as the verb that follows it.
modal.avere: When the next verb takes avere.
modal.essere: When the next verb takes essere.

motion-goal.label: Movement to a place, or movement itself
motion-goal.technical: A verb of movement. It takes essere when a destination or direction is stated, and avere when the activity itself or its duration is the point.
motion-goal.explanation: With a place the movement goes to, this verb takes essere. When it describes the activity on its own, for example how long it lasted, it takes avere.
motion-goal.avere: The activity itself, or how long it lasted.
motion-goal.essere: A destination or direction is stated.

compound.label: Follows the base verb
compound.technical: A verb built by adding a prefix to another verb. It takes the auxiliary of the verb named in `derivedFrom`.
compound.explanation: This verb is built on another verb and takes the same auxiliary as that verb.

reflexive.label: Reflexive verb
reflexive.technical: A reflexive or pronominal verb always takes essere. Applied in the code from the verb's -si ending, so no verb has an entry for it.
reflexive.explanation: A reflexive verb always takes essere.

default.label: Takes avere
default.technical: A verb with no entry in the auxiliaries file takes avere.

common.label: Common variant
common.explanation: An equal modern variant, shown beside the standard form.

colloquial.label: Colloquial
colloquial.explanation: Used in everyday speech, avoided in writing.

formal.label: Formal
formal.explanation: Used in careful or official writing, closer to the Latin root.

regional.label: Regional
regional.explanation: Used in one area or dialect, not standard elsewhere.

dated.label: Dated
dated.explanation: Sounds old-fashioned to a modern speaker, but still used.

archaic.label: Archaic
archaic.explanation: Rarely used except deliberately, for effect.

obsolete.label: Obsolete
obsolete.explanation: No longer in real use. Found only in historical texts.

sense.label: Different meaning
sense.explanation: A different meaning of the verb.

clipped_common.label: Clipped, everyday
clipped_common.explanation: A shortened form in everyday use.

clipped_poetic.label: Clipped, poetic
clipped_poetic.explanation: A shortened form found in poetry and song.
